restoration_note: Teaching describes Adam as the threefold-sealed icon-bearer (icon of the Ambassador, five-fold molding after heaven and the Five Sons, seal of the entire cosmos) and elaborates seven reasons why the natural man was so fashioned. Most fills are tightly constrained: trace-anchored name (ⲁⲇⲁⲙ), split lexemes across line breaks (ⲣ̄-ⲉⲯⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ, ⲉⲡⲉⲓⲁⲏ, ⲡⲉϥⲧⲱⲃⲉ), formula completions (ⲭⲉⲕⲁⲁⲥ ⲛ̄, ⲡⲉϩⲕⲱⲧ ⲉ-), and parallel-formula recovery (ⲛ̄ⲥⲉⲭⲓⲟⲩⲱ from line 31). The 4-char lacuna {16} is the only gap with no trace or close formula; restored conservatively as ⲁⲣⲉⲍ (guard/keep) on the basis of the reading's patronage-and-shelter sense, but flagged low.

restorations.basis: Editor's restoration anchored on partial traces ⲁⲇ-; the molded natural man is identified with the First Man at the head of the threefold enumeration. Confirms the reading's frame: 'in Adam, the First Man' as the icon-bearer.
Standard Lycopolitan relative converter ⲉⲧ- linking ⲡⲓⲛⲉ ('likeness') to the qualitative ⲡⲣⲓ̈ⲉ ('radiant') in the next line: 'the likeness which is radiant of the icon.' Grammatically required.

Editor's restoration confirmed by trace -ⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ. ⲍⲓⲧⲛ̄ (Lyc. = Sah. ϩⲓⲧⲛ̄) + ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ ('the Light') fits the reading: Adam molded 'through the Light of the firstborn-state of heaven,' i.e., shaped by the descending illumination of Divine Truth.

Editor's ⲡⲕⲁⲍ paired with preceding ⲧⲡⲉ ('heaven') is constrained by the standard Manichaean cosmographical pair; the connector ⲙⲛ̄ ('and') is the most natural link to ⲡⲧⲟⲩ ⲛ̄ϣⲏⲣⲉ. Apparatus notes some characters of the connector remain uncertain.

Editor's restoration: completes ⲡⲉϩⲕⲱⲧ ('his structure') split across the line-break (line 14 ends ⲡⲉϩ-) plus relative converter ⲉ- introducing the qualitative ϣⲃⲓ̈ⲁⲓ̈ⲧ. Confirmed by the parallel ⲡⲟⲩⲕⲱⲧ ϣⲃⲓ̈ⲁⲓ̈ⲧ in the next line.
Editor's restoration of standard Greek causal subordinator ἐπειδή; introduces the explanatory clause about the structure of all creatures being altered relative to Adam's. Frequent in the Kephalaia.
Editor's restoration; Lycopolitan intensive pronoun ⲛ̄ⲧⲁϩ (= Sah. ⲛ̄ⲧⲟϥ) 'himself,' emphasizing Adam as singular subject. Standard usage; pronoun is reinforced by the same word ⲛ̄ⲧⲁϩ in line 24.
Editor's restoration of initial ⲍ- of ⲍⲁⲩ ('bitter'); completes the explicit contrast 'beautiful'/'bitter' affections drawn upward to life vs. downward to death (lines 29-31).
Editor's restoration; completes the Greek loan ἐξουσία (ⲣ̄-ⲉⲯⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ 'exercise authority'), with -ⲉⲯⲟⲩ at end of line 31 and -ⲓⲁ visible at start of line 32; the medial ⲥ falls in the gap.
Editor's restoration; the trace ⲙ̄- begins the genitive linker, and the reading confirms 'abase in him the cosmos entire' — Adam as compact form of the whole cosmic circuit, the seal of the cosmos.

Editor's restoration; standard Manichaean cosmological term, the demiurges/archons who 'appointed and fashioned Adam' that they may rule. Matches the reading's frame ('the proprium-powers fashioned Adam') and parallels ⲛⲁⲏⲙⲓⲟⲩⲣⲅⲟⲥ in earlier lines.
Editor's restoration; ⲍⲏⲧϩ̄ completes the ⲛ̄- preserved at end of line 35 ('lord in him'); ⲛⲥⲉ-ⲭⲓⲟⲩⲱ ('and they take precedence') exactly parallels ⲛ̄ⲥⲉⲭⲓⲟⲩⲱ ⲛ̄ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲣ̄ⲣⲟ in line 32.

Editor's restoration; visible -ⲁⲏ matches Lycopolitan spelling ⲉⲡⲉⲓⲁⲏ for ἐπειδή. ⲉⲡⲉⲓ + preserved ⲁⲏ completes the causal subordinator that introduces 'they all desired the likeness of the icon of the Ambassador.'

Editor's restoration; copular pronoun ⲛ̄ⲧⲁϥ in the construction ⲛ̄ⲧⲁϥ ⲡⲉ ('he is') predicating Adam as 'an imprint-figure of seal and a new character' (the fourth reason: Adam stamps the new character upon all generation).

Editor's restoration; completes the standard purpose-clause idiom ⲭⲉⲕⲁⲁⲥ ('in order that') — the visible ⲭⲉ- at end of line 51 preserves the head of the formula. ⲛ̄ links to the following nominal subject ⲭⲡⲟ ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ ('all the begettings').

Editor's restoration completing ⲡⲉϥⲧⲱⲃⲉ ('his imprint/seal'); preserved ⲡⲉϥⲧ- + ⲱⲃⲉ. Confirmed by the same lexeme ⲧⲱⲃⲉ at line 50/51 ('imprint-figure of seal'); 'all begettings shall be begotten before his imprint' — the fourth reason.

Lacuna est. 4 chars. The reading at this point describes the sixth reason: 'a great patronage (πατρωνία) shall come to be... those of above shall [protect/guard], and the other archons shall not do any evil on account of Adam.' Lyc. ⲁⲣⲉⲍ (= Sah. ⲁⲣⲉϩ, 'keep, guard, protect') fits the 4-char count and the patronage-and-shelter sense; the active subject 'those of above' guard those bearing the icon. Conservative fill — alternatives like ⲣⲱⲓⲥ ('watch over') would also fit the count.
